subject_entity.notes: Tertullian's treatise c. 206-212 defending the reality of Christ's incarnation against docetists and Marcion; argues that Christ took real human flesh from the virgin Mary.

object_entity.notes: First major Latin Christian author; active in Carthage c. 195–220. Wrote at least 31 works spanning apologetics, anti-heretical polemic, and moral discipline. Coined 'trinitas' and 'tres personae una substantia'. Defender of apostolic succession, rule of faith, incarnation, and bodily resurrection. Later attracted to Montanist rigorism c. 207; teacher of Cyprian by doctrinal influence.

passage.excerpt: The Son of God was crucified; I am not ashamed because men must needs be ashamed of it. And the Son of God died; it is by all means to be believed because it is absurd. And he was buried and rose again; the fact is certain because it is impossible. But how will all this be true in him, if he was not himself true — if he had not truly in himself that which might be crucified, might die, might be buried and might rise again? This is the flesh suffused with blood, built up with bones, interwoven with nerves, entwined with veins.
passage.notes: Certum est quia impossibile; defense of the reality of Christ's flesh and incarnation; anti-docetist
